4. Opposite party No. 1 contested the application by filing affidavit in opposition denying the statements of the petitioner. It is stated in the affidavit-in-opposition that upon publication of the opposite party's trade marks in the Trade marks Journal No. 109 for January, 1988, the petitioner filed an opposition, which was subsequently declared abandoned and accordingly, registration was effective in respect of the opposite party's application. It is contended on behalf of opposite party No. 1 that the petitioner did not avail the remedy provided by section 76 of the Act by filing any appeal against the order of the Registrar of Trade. Marks. It is further contended that the words "NABICO" and "NABISCO" have no similarity either visually or phonetically and, therefore, would not lead to any deception so far as the consumers are concerned. It is further stated that the opposite party has been using the trademark for the last ninteen and half (19-1/2 years and has acquired a very good reputation and goodwill in the market and, as such, the application for rectification is barred by limitation and also barred under the principle of estoppel, waiver and acquiescence by conduct. It is contended that the mark registered by opposite party No.1 comprises the monogram of the letter B inside a crescent moon with a star and the device of a lady, deer, pineapple, coconut and the word Nabico নেবিকো both in English and in Bengali along with other distinguishing features with particular colour design, device and get-up printed on the wrapper and label in respect of lozenge and, as such, the mark of the opposite party has no similarity with that of the petitioner. 

 13. Now let us consider the length of use by opposite party No. 1 of his trade mark and the bar of limitation under section 24 of the Act.
